nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and $u$, $v$ sentential forms of $g$. If the concatenation $uv$ yields the terminal word $w$ through a derivation forest of height at most $n$, then there are terminal words $w_1$, $w_2$ with $w = w_1 w_2$ such that $u$ yields $w_1$ and $v$ yields $w_2$, each through a derivation forest of height at most $n$.
nodes.title: Splitting a height-bounded yield at a concatenation

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If a sentential form $u$ yields the terminal word $w_1$ through a derivation forest of height at most $n$, and a sentential form $v$ yields the terminal word $w_2$ through one of height at most $m$, then the concatenation $uv$ yields $w_1 w_2$ through a derivation forest of height at most $\max(n, m)$.
nodes.title: Concatenating height-bounded yields

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If a sentential form $\alpha$ yields the terminal word $w$, then there is a natural number $n$ such that $\alpha$ yields $w$ through a derivation forest of height at most $n$, but through no derivation forest of height at most $m$ for any $m < n$.
nodes.title: Minimal-height derivation forests exist

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar, $A$ a nonterminal and $l$, $r$, $x$ terminal words. Suppose that for every terminal word $w$ yielded by $A$ the word $l w r$ is also yielded by $A$, and that $A$ yields $x$. Then for every natural number $i$ the nonterminal $A$ yields $l^i x r^i$, where $l^i$ and $r^i$ denote the concatenations of $i$ copies of $l$ and of $r$.
nodes.title: Pumping through a self-context

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and $R$ a natural number such that every production of $g$ has an output of length at most $R$. If a sentential form $\alpha$ yields the terminal word $w$ through a derivation forest of height at most $n$, then $|w| \le |\alpha| \cdot \max(2, R)^n$.
nodes.title: Length bound for height-bounded yields

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If a sentential form $\alpha$ yields the terminal word $w$ through a derivation forest of height at most $n$, and $n \le m$, then $\alpha$ yields $w$ through a derivation forest of height at most $m$.
nodes.title: Raising the height bound of a yield

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and $A \to \alpha_1 B \alpha_2$ a production of $g$, where $B$ is a nonterminal and $\alpha_1$, $\alpha_2$ are sentential forms. If $\alpha_1$ yields the terminal word $l$ and $\alpha_2$ yields the terminal word $r$, then for every terminal word $w$ yielded by $B$ the word $l w r$ is yielded by $A$; that is, $(l, r)$ is a derivation context from $A$ to $B$.
nodes.title: A production gives derivation contexts

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If a sentential form $\alpha$ yields the terminal word $w$ through a derivation forest of height at most $n$, then $\alpha$ yields $w$.
nodes.title: Height-bounded yields are yields

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If a sentential form $\alpha$ yields the terminal word $w$, then there is a natural number $n$ such that $\alpha$ yields $w$ through a derivation forest of height at most $n$.
nodes.title: Every yield has a height bound

nodes.summary: For every context-free language $L$ over an alphabet $T$ there is a natural number $n > 0$ such that every word $w \in L$ with $|w| \ge n$ can be written as $w = uvxyz$ with words $u, v, x, y, z$ over $T$ such that $vy$ is nonempty, $|vxy| \le n$, and $u v^i x y^i z \in L$ for every natural number $i$, where $v^i$ and $y^i$ denote the concatenations of $i$ copies of $v$ and of $y$.
nodes.title: Pumping lemma for context-free languages

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar, let $A$ and $B$ be nonterminals of $g$, and let $l$ and $r$ be words over the terminal alphabet. Then $(l, r)$ is a derivation context from $A$ to $B$ when, for every terminal word $w$ that the nonterminal $B$ yields in $g$, the nonterminal $A$ yields the word $l w r$ in $g$.
nodes.title: Derivation contexts

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. For a sentential form $\alpha$ (a list of terminals and nonterminals of $g$), a terminal word $w$ and a natural number $n$, say that $\alpha$ yields $w$ at height $n$ when this follows from three rules: the empty form yields the empty word at every height $n$; if $\alpha$ yields $w$ at height $n$, then for every terminal $a$ the form $a\alpha$ yields $aw$ at height $n$; and if…
nodes.title: Height-bounded derivations

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
